# Everyone Hates Elon

**Everyone Hates Elon** (EHE) is a **UK-based activist group** formed in early 2025 that conducts guerrilla campaigns against entrepreneur **Elon Musk** . The group emerged in response to Musk's political interventions in British affairs, including his support for far-right activist Tommy Robinson and his controversial gesture at Donald Trump's second inauguration that many interpreted as a Nazi salute .

The group's activities have gained significant media attention and social media virality, with their "Swasticar" campaign targeting Tesla vehicles and their posters appearing across London . Their efforts have coincided with a notable decline in Tesla sales, with European sales dropping 45% in January 2025 .

## Formation and Background

**Everyone Hates Elon** was founded by a "very small group of friends" who were outraged by Musk's interventions in British politics . The group members, who are scattered across the UK and had worked on campaigns before, were particularly offended by Musk's demands for new elections in the UK and his campaign to free Tommy Robinson from prison . Robinson is a controversial figure who founded the English Defense League, described as a fascist political party .

The group's formation was further catalyzed by Musk's appearance at Trump's inauguration in January 2025, where he made a gesture that many interpreted as a Nazi salute . This incident, combined with his growing political influence as head of the Department of Government Efficiency (DOGE) in the Trump administration, provided the "impetus they needed" to launch their campaign .

## Campaign Activities and Tactics

### The "Swasticar" Campaign

The group's most prominent campaign centers on the "Swasticar" theme, which plays on the word "Swastika" (the Nazi symbol) and "Tesla" . Their 标志性海报 featured a Tesla vehicle with the caption "Goes from 0 to 1939 in 3 seconds" (a reference to the start of World War II), followed by "The Swasticar" . The image paired this with a photograph of Musk making his controversial gesture at Trump's inauguration .

The campaign has expanded beyond posters to include **"Swasticar" stickers** that members have plastered on hundreds of Tesla vehicles across London . The group has also taken a cardboard cutout of Musk to Tesla dealerships as part of their protests .

### Guerrilla Advertising Campaign

The group has deployed **unconventional marketing tactics** to spread their message throughout London, with their reach extending beyond the capital city . Their activities have included:

* Posting anti-Musk advertisements on London bus stops and the London Underground 

* Creating posters that read "Delete your account. If the bar lets Nazis in, it's a Nazi bar" targeting Musk's social media platform X

* Launching "Elon Musk is a bellend" merchandise, including t-shirts

One particularly notable poster featured the text "Elon Musk is a bellend. Signed, the UK" . A group spokesperson explained this messaging by saying: "Elon Musk has all the money in the world – but he can't buy popularity. The British public hates his guts and polling shows we don't want him interfering in our politics anymore. We thought we'd communicate that to him in a way only British people could – by calling him a bellend" .

### Fundraising and Donation Strategy

**Everyone Hates Elon** runs a fundraising campaign called **"People Versus Elon"** on crowdfunding platforms . Their initial goal was to raise £50,000, with the stated intention that "the more we raise, the more we can do" . The campaign is anticipated to raise £150,000 over one year .

A unique aspect of their fundraising strategy involves a pledge system where donors commit to giving a small amount (such as one penny) for each post Musk makes on X . With Musk posting approximately 2,000 times monthly and close to 1,000 people making regular pledges, the initiative is on track to meet its fundraising goals .

The group has stated that all proceeds go directly toward the costs of their campaigning . They have raised over £4,300 (approximately $8,800) as of March 2025 <reference type="end" id=37>, and in an interview with The Hollywood Reporter, they claimed to have raised close to $200,000 and donated the funds "to causes \[Elon] hates" .

## Impact and Reception

### Media Attention and Virality

The group's activities have achieved **significant media attention and social media virality**. Their TikTok videos have garnered millions of views, with one particular video showing the installation of their "Swasticar" poster accumulating over 9 million views and 980,000 likes . The campaign has been covered by numerous international media outlets including The Hollywood Reporter, PinkNews, The New Daily, and The Independent .

The group has leveraged their newfound virality to raise awareness and funds for causes they believe Musk would oppose, including Everyday Racism and Rainbow Migration .

### Effect on Tesla Sales

The timing of the **Everyone Hates Elon** campaign has coincided with a significant decline in Tesla sales, particularly in Europe. According to data from the European Automobile Manufacturers' Association (ACEA), Tesla sold just 9,945 vehicles in Europe in January 2025, representing a **45% drop** from 18,161 units in January 2024 . The company's market share in Europe shrank from 1.8% to 1% .

In Australia, Tesla sales plummeted 71.9% in February 2025 compared to the previous year, with just 1,592 vehicles sold compared to 5,665 in the same period in 2024 . Globally, Tesla's first-quarter 2025 vehicle deliveries dropped 13% year-over-year to 336,681 units, marking the company's lowest quarterly performance since mid-2022 and the largest drop in the company's history .

Industry analysts have suggested that the decline in sales may be linked to what they describe as a shift in the Tesla brand's image. As James Obiegbu and Gretchen Larsen wrote: "Owning a Tesla may no longer signal purely \[a buyer's] beliefs about sustainability. There may be a nod to political or ideological affiliations that do not align with their own" .

### Public Response and Protests

The **Everyone Hates Elon** campaign has inspired similar protest movements and actions against Musk and Tesla. A broader movement called **"Tesla Takedown"** has emerged, with demonstrations in over 250 cities worldwide . This grassroots initiative organized nonviolent protests at Tesla locations across the US, Canada, Europe, and Australia, calling for boycotts and urging the public to divest from Tesla by selling their vehicles and shares .

Some protests have escalated beyond peaceful demonstrations. There have been reports of vandalism at Tesla facilities, including charging stations and vehicles . For example, on March 24, 2025, incendiary devices were discovered at a Tesla dealership in Austin, Texas .

The campaign has also highlighted growing public sentiment against Musk. A February 2025 poll indicated that 62% of respondents viewed Musk's role in government as "inappropriate," and 44% felt it damaged confidence in the administration's reform efforts . In the UK, a poll showed that 69% of the public believe Musk is having a negative impact on UK politics .

## Notability and Assessment

The **Everyone Hates Elon** campaign meets several criteria for notability in the context of contemporary activism and social movements:

1. **Media Coverage**: The group has received extensive coverage from multiple reputable international media outlets, including The Hollywood Reporter, PinkNews, The New Daily, and The Independent .

2. **Social Media Impact**: Their content has achieved significant virality, with TikTok videos garnering millions of views and widespread sharing across social media platforms .

3. **Organizational Structure**: The group has demonstrated organizational capacity through their coordinated campaigns, fundraising efforts, and consistent messaging across multiple platforms .

4. **Measurable Impact**: The campaign has coincided with significant declines in Tesla sales, particularly in European markets, suggesting a measurable economic impact .

5. **Influence on Public Discourse**: The group's activities have contributed to broader discussions about wealth inequality, corporate influence, and political activism in the digital age .

## Criticisms and Counterarguments

While the **Everyone Hates Elon** campaign has gained significant attention and support, it has also faced criticism and counterarguments:

1. **Accusations of Bias**: Critics have argued that the group's name itself demonstrates a lack of neutrality and presents a biased perspective . The group makes no attempt to hide their opposition to Musk, stating their goal is to "piss Elon Musk off, one small action at a time" .

2. **Tactical Concerns**: Some have questioned the effectiveness and appropriateness of their tactics, particularly the use of the "Swasticar" theme, which critics argue may minimize the historical significance of the Nazi symbol .

3. **Economic Impact Questions**: While Tesla sales have declined, some analysts have suggested that other factors, including production updates and market competition, may have contributed to the decline alongside the campaign .

4. **Target Audience Limitations**: The group's messaging, particularly their use of British colloquialisms like "bellend," may limit their appeal and effectiveness outside of specific cultural contexts .

## Legacy and Future Prospects

The **Everyone Hates Elon** campaign represents a notable example of **grassroots digital activism** in the 21st century. Their use of social media, guerrilla marketing tactics, and crowdfunding has allowed a small group of friends to achieve international attention and potentially influence corporate behavior .

The campaign has also highlighted broader societal tensions around:

* The political influence of billionaires

* The intersection of technology, business, and politics

* The role of social media in activism and protest movements

* The relationship between consumer choice and political expression

As of 2025, the group continues to be active, with plans for further campaigns and an expanded reach. Their success in achieving media attention and measurable impact suggests that their model of **small-scale, high-impact activism** may inspire similar movements in the future.

The campaign's long-term legacy will likely be determined by whether it can sustain its momentum and achieve its stated goals of reducing Musk's political influence and promoting causes that align with their values. Regardless of the ultimate outcome, **Everyone Hates Elon** has demonstrated how digital platforms and creative activism can amplify the voice of small groups and potentially challenge the power of even the world's wealthiest individuals.

The individual told the outlet that the group is made up of “a very small group of friends” who are scattered across the U.K.

The friends had worked on campaigns before and were all outraged at **Musk’s interventions into British politics earlier this year**. “We saw Elon Musk sticking his oar in and demanding new elections in the U.K., campaigning to free Tommy Robinson from prison,” said the member of EHE. Tommy Robinson is an infamous white supremacist who in 2009 founded the fascist political party, the**English Defense League**.

One of the initial efforts launched by the EHE was a fundraiser, dubbed People Versus Elon, wherein donations could be made per post on X made by the platform’s billionaire. Even if each time, a person had pledged pennies, the group told the Hollywood Reporter that they raised close to**$200,000 and donated the funds** “to causes [Elon] hates.”

Today, the group uses Instagram, TikTok, and BlueSky to update followers on their activities. After local elections held in the U.K., where the far-right party, Reform U.K., performed well, **EHE has placed billboards and posters featuring Nigel Farage—**who has had his own problems with Musk.

The origins of Everyone Hates Elon
----------------------------------

The group, however, really got started with stickers, with a photo of Musk, with the caption “Don’t Buy a Swatsticar,” alluding to Musk’s Nazi salute during the presidential innoguration activities.

Related stories
---------------

“So we saw Elon Musk doing that salute at Donald Trump’s inauguration,“ said the EHE member, explaining that watching Musk’s full integration into far-right politics made many feel like they ”had to do something.“ The campaigners had assumed that their audience would be based in the U.K., but noted in the interview that people from **Europe, the US, Canada, and Australia have all placed orders for stickers**. The EHE member said that their work had led them to believe that ”there is a global movement of people who won’t stand for his fascism and nonsense."

10.title: Who's behind the anti-Musk tube ads?
10.description: Plus: discontent on Eel Pie Island and where to get the perfect £7 martini
10.content:
Dear Londoners — Are you a Murphy’s true-believer or a Guinness diehard? Either way, we hope you’ve recovered from whatever you were drinking on the St Patrick’s Day weekend (although things aren’t finished quite yet, of course — we’ll see you in the Auld Shillelagh tonight for round two).

Here at The Londoner, we have another reason to celebrate. Last week, we had a bunch of new members join us from stories as diverse as the abandoned modernist [penguin pool](https://www.the-londoner.co.uk/lubetkin-penguin-pool/) at London Zoo, Westminster City Council’s new [nightlife plan](https://www.the-londoner.co.uk/can-we-save-soho/) for Soho and the tragic suicide of a [London doctor](https://www.the-londoner.co.uk/nhs-doctor-suicides-jagdip-sidhu/) and what his death says about the state of the NHS.So hello to these new supporters — we’re so happy to have you onboard.

If you’re yet to take the plunge into a paying membership, now is your chance. Click the links below to get access to a time-limited 20% off deal:

Keep reading for your Monday briefing, a collection of London’s biggest stories and the best spots to eat, drink and hang out.

* * *

### **Big story:****Who’s behind the protest adverts taking over the tube?**

**Topline:** A series of satirical adverts criticising Elon Musk and Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu have appeared at bus stations and on tube trains across the capital.

**Context:** While they use the same tactics, the guerrilla political adverts are actually the work of two different campaigns. The first has posted a series of adverts criticising US billionaire and close Trump ally Elon Musk, after he made a series of high-profile interventions in British politics including calling for the release of far-right extremist Tommy Robinson, accusing Labour MP Jess Phillips of being a “genocide rape apologist” and trying to force a new election in the UK.

[![Image 1: A sign at a bus stop declares, Elon Musk is a bellend, Signed, the UK.](https://lh7-rt.googleusercontent.com/docsz/AD_4nXe9W9wBZFm8AKAVwPbKHz4LxYovPQZBzp7u549Td-VU9fdKWTPFvChNp2rpZp7MahEnTKSDwBn52kgSAPlgCj5ltuHko9UpOWFIOr-n32S_eAEDUdrkNg1pAiJg04jR0-vx9Sp6?key=ML4ur5QVRGR4y2IPxSTmTHfr)](https://lh7-rt.googleusercontent.com/docsz/AD_4nXe9W9wBZFm8AKAVwPbKHz4LxYovPQZBzp7u549Td-VU9fdKWTPFvChNp2rpZp7MahEnTKSDwBn52kgSAPlgCj5ltuHko9UpOWFIOr-n32S_eAEDUdrkNg1pAiJg04jR0-vx9Sp6?key=ML4ur5QVRGR4y2IPxSTmTHfr)

Image courtesy of Everyone Hates Elon via Instagram

Meanwhile, on Wednesday last week, some 200 faux-Labour-Party adverts appeared at bus stations and Jubilee line trains accusing the government of “doing deals with war criminals”, featuring pictures of foreign secretary David Lammy and Israeli prime minister Netanyahu. Many were still on the network over the weekend.

[![Image 2: A poster with a picture of two men shaking hands, with explosions and a jet in the background, reads With Labour, Britain is doing deals with war criminals, with the Labour Party rose logo and the hashtag #IsraelTradeDeal displayed at the bottom](https://www.the-londoner.co.uk/content/images/2025/03/image-6-1.png)](https://www.the-londoner.co.uk/content/images/2025/03/image-6-1.png)

Image courtesy of Byline Times

**Who’s behind it?:** A group named Everyone Hates Elon has taken responsibility for the series of anti-Musk ads, saying “he’s a gruesome man, and we all need to come together to stop him having this incredible influence over all of our lives”. Its members have all stayed anonymous, but claim they’re a collective from across the country who are angry at the American tech billionaire’s increasing interventions in British politics to advocate for extreme right wing causes. They’re using the campaign and its newfound virality to raise thousands of pounds for a range of charities that they feel the billionaire would dislike, including Everyday Racism and Rainbow Migration.

[Byline Times](https://bylinetimes.com/2025/03/13/guerrilla-ad-campaign-attacks-uk-government-for-doing-trade-talks-with-israel-war-criminals/?ref=the-londoner.co.uk) spoke to an anonymous member of the group behind the anti-Netanyahu ads, who argued that “trade relations are one of the few sources of leverage that the UK holds over Israel that could put pressure on it to end its genocidal violence in Gaza”.

**Are they sanctioned by TfL?**: No. The adverts weren’t paid for — they’d likely break TfL’s rules on political advertising anyway — but were illegally papered over pre-existing adverts. The transport network says it removes all such fake adverts as soon as they are notified of their presence, but campaigners seem to be putting new ones up as quickly as the network is taking them down.

**How are they doing it?**: The campaigns are relatively easy to pull off, given how reliant on printed adverts the capital’s transport network is. On the bus network, TfL manages nearly ten thousand different advertising boards, over 90% of which are print, [according to the network](https://tfl.gov.uk/info-for/media/press-releases/2024/september/tfl-selects-global-and-jcdecaux-to-manage-its-world-leading-advertising-contracts?ref=the-londoner.co.uk#:~:text=JCDecaux%20will%20continue%20to%20manage,and%20612%20digital%20advertising%20panels.). It’s a similar case on the tube, where the almost all ads are still printed too. Those kinds of adverts can be slotted over by your own new artwork; just a few years ago a network of guerrilla ad campaigners actually put up posters explaining the process to anyone who fancied joining their ranks.

[![Image 3: A subway ad details how to hack this ad space by designing artwork in the correct size, sliding the artwork over an existing ad, and taking and sharing the picture online with the hashtags #AdHackManifesto and #AdvertisingShitsInYourHead](https://lh7-rt.googleusercontent.com/docsz/AD_4nXdQ7OobuK7p3wy5qvj1WQcAJD8M3owGHGSKNS-U2IPd-IK0zLArD-VUfI9J3t4hEcPjqzcs7HccrO7M2LvBHjcBZHncOCPyvtKusPmsLfUQ83nRNg9G96b03qFWfjdPbIb8o9MZ?key=ML4ur5QVRGR4y2IPxSTmTHfr)](https://lh7-rt.googleusercontent.com/docsz/AD_4nXdQ7OobuK7p3wy5qvj1WQcAJD8M3owGHGSKNS-U2IPd-IK0zLArD-VUfI9J3t4hEcPjqzcs7HccrO7M2LvBHjcBZHncOCPyvtKusPmsLfUQ83nRNg9G96b03qFWfjdPbIb8o9MZ?key=ML4ur5QVRGR4y2IPxSTmTHfr)

Image: Image courtesy of Special Patrol Group via X

**A long history?**: It’s far from the first time this sort of campaign has happened. There was a [series of anti-Israel posters put up in 2018](https://www.london.gov.uk/who-we-are/what-london-assembly-does/questions-mayor/find-an-answer/guerrilla-advertising-tfl-bus-stops?ref=the-londoner.co.uk), and multiple rounds of satirical anti-Conservative party campaigns in the build-up to past elections.

* * *

### Your news briefing

🏝️Residents of Eel Pie Island — the secretive, star-studded island near Twickenham accessible only by footbridge — fear that a [planning report](https://www.theguardian.com/politics/2025/mar/16/loved-by-rockers-and-royals-eel-pie-island-is-threatened-by-tide-of-red-tape?ref=the-londoner.co.uk) by Richmond council will destroy their community. Due to be released today, the document may reclassify the island as a flood zone, meaning locals won’t be able to insure or remortgage their homes.

🍺 Another one bites the dust… The Gun, the beloved Homerton pub and club space, has shuttered due to “unsustainable” trading conditions, says co-founder Nick Stephens. Opened in 2014, the space quickly became an East London fixture for DJs and buzzy food pop-ups. Stephens and fellow landlord Hanna Sinclair-Stephens will now focus on their other pub, the Compton Arms in Canonbury (interestingly, that venue has also faced [much-publicised challenges](https://www.mylondon.news/whats-on/whats-on-news/old-compton-arms-survives-closure-25257379?ref=the-londoner.co.uk) to stay open in the past few years).

📱Phone thefts are increasingly common in the capital — one every eight minutes, according to recent figures — but it’s difficult to find out what actually happens next. [The Sunday Times found out](https://www.thetimes.com/article/6ba959cf-9ad7-4ea1-9aca-bb750a94079d?shareToken=05f4c59df87bf1be505a8e9fcbeb5eea&ref=the-londoner.co.uk), by tracking the end locations of thousands of stolen phones and found that 80% end up abroad. The most common end points were Algeria (28% of cases), China (20% of cases) and Hong Kong (7%).

* * *

**If you missed it,**over the weekend we published Andrew Kersley’s heartwrenching long-read telling the life and death of Dr Jagdip Sidhu, an NHS doctor from Harrow who took their own life after years of working in an underfunded, broken healthcare system. One NHS doctor takes their own life every three weeks.

Readers called it “heartbreaking” and “one of the most moving and powerful pieces I’ve read”. Make sure to read [the full story here](https://www.the-londoner.co.uk/nhs-doctor-suicides-jagdip-sidhu/).

[![Image 4: Lewisham NHS Trust sign with a stethoscope hanging from it, and two birds in flight above](https://lh7-rt.googleusercontent.com/docsz/AD_4nXdbGbXBuvPUN-NB23Pt8Mro97u8Q3s5lKomgDPYWX5OVs324h6upO0CbUm8UwbItlQTzz20oMMylE_hbbT16F2AvUFCsGZTK5g9mxKBT8GIMK_BFLjB0saWcdpCf8qCAzw82wlw?key=ML4ur5QVRGR4y2IPxSTmTHfr)](https://lh7-rt.googleusercontent.com/docsz/AD_4nXdbGbXBuvPUN-NB23Pt8Mro97u8Q3s5lKomgDPYWX5OVs324h6upO0CbUm8UwbItlQTzz20oMMylE_hbbT16F2AvUFCsGZTK5g9mxKBT8GIMK_BFLjB0saWcdpCf8qCAzw82wlw?key=ML4ur5QVRGR4y2IPxSTmTHfr)

Illustration by The Londoner/Jake Greenhalgh

* * *

### **Wining and dining**

_With endless offerings and non-stop openings, we all know that deciding where to eat and drink in the capital can be fraught. We want to make it easy — so every week we’ll give you our insider guide to the city’s best spots._

**One perfect meal:**

Camberwell’s Church Street has become increasingly buzzy in the last couple of years. Hello JoJo, a new “bakery, brunch and dinner” spot is replacing the recently departed Forza Wine; while the Camberwell Arms continues to serve up the most in-demand roast in the entirety of South London. But that doesn’t mean some of the road’s excellent old-timers should be neglected, either — and Van Hing, an unpretentious Vietnamese cafe and restaurant, is one of them. The exterior is perfect, unchanged for years: shades of verdant green with flamboyant, 70s-style yellow lettering announcing its name. Inside, it’s charmingly old-school, with paper tablecloths and Vietnamese pastoral scenes and faux-ivy climbing up the pillars.

As for the food, Van Hing is wonderful alone or as a couple, but it really comes into its own in a group — it has one of those hundred-piece menus, so buy to share. We recommend the Nhân Chay, a traditional fried vietnamese crispy pancake filled with vegetables, the summer rolls, the sizzling aubergine and the salt and pepper squid, with a phở to follow.

**One perfect drink:**

The photos are always the same: a hot dog, daubed in giallo-red ketchup and lurid yellow mustard, posed next to an elegant, olive-laden martini. Once you’ve noticed the mismatch turning up in your social media feed, you won’t be able to stop — this weekend, The Londoner counted five appearances of the phenomenon. The cause? Rasputin’s, a new(ish) bar from the wildly successful team behind Dom’s Subs, which has quickly become the place to see, be seen and, most importantly, have a good time.

[![Image 5: Two hotdogs topped with onions and a cocktail glass with olives on a green menu at Rasputin's bar](https://www.the-londoner.co.uk/content/images/2025/03/image-7.png)](https://www.the-londoner.co.uk/content/images/2025/03/image-7.png)

Image by @worldsfamousgordos/@rasputinsbar via Instagram

Although the hot dogs are only part of the appeal, they encapsulate the bar’s wider promise, which is something cheap and a little silly and nevertheless extremely good — a marriage of kitsch and quality that’s easy to love. The five-olive martinis are £7, the lagers are a fiver, the margaritas are a tenner, thrillingly well-priced for this area of post-gentrification Hackney (and for London as a whole).

Bathed in red light, Rasputin’s has the stagey sleaziness, the camp sexiness of a winking neon sign. It makes you “feel like you’re in the Roadhouse from Twin Peaks”, as food and drink writer [Lauren O’Neill wrote.](https://diningout.substack.com/p/dining-out-023-rasputins?ref=the-londoner.co.uk) Put more simply: It’s fun. So slurp the ketchup off your fingers, buy another round and promise not to get home before midnight.

* * *

### **Ins and outs**

_Ins_: Cheap daffodils, the £12.50 three-oysters-and-wine deal at 80-20 Wines in Peckham, Taste of Peshawar in Stonebridge Park, Murphy’s stout, karaoke at Viet Quan, pre-stretching your shoes at the cobbler, cigars at the Piccadilly Hippodrome, the Cock Tavern, rewatching _Attack the Block_ (2011), small plates (they went out, and now they’re back in again — sorry!), FM Mangal flatbreads.

_Outs_: False starts to spring, cover charges, suitcases on the Tube, TikToks on public transport, the Cow in Notting Hill, bars decorated to look like someone’s flat (House Party, the Little Yellow Door et al.), moaning about Clapham, pre-booking systems for lidos, £7 plates of padron peppers.

* * *

### **Our favourite reads**

[**‘The ghosts are everywhere’: can the British Museum survive its omni-crisis?**](https://www.theguardian.com/culture/2025/jan/16/the-ghosts-are-everywhere-can-the-british-museum-survive-its-omni-crisis?ref=the-londoner.co.uk)**— Charlotte Higgins, _Guardian_**

Earlier this year, the Guardian published a deep dive into the state of the British Museum. After a spate of high profile thefts, controversies over its funding from oil giants like BP and growing demands for objects taken by colonisers to be returned to the countries they came from, what does the future look like for the country’s namesake museum?

[![Image 6: View of the Great Court in the British Museum](https://lh7-rt.googleusercontent.com/docsz/AD_4nXezzdBh6sWXdDnsUXkDQHJvF-7NRWjrq9JAZcz6z5TCQs9NjJDYp3ZpQVvpdc6Wi4oA0rHtF8JEG26a3egHLEem6pTLKwsGdgaj9tilIhUsOJ7O7bvqDIfoWc4a8JupkBgmjc_Y?key=ML4ur5QVRGR4y2IPxSTmTHfr)](https://lh7-rt.googleusercontent.com/docsz/AD_4nXezzdBh6sWXdDnsUXkDQHJvF-7NRWjrq9JAZcz6z5TCQs9NjJDYp3ZpQVvpdc6Wi4oA0rHtF8JEG26a3egHLEem6pTLKwsGdgaj9tilIhUsOJ7O7bvqDIfoWc4a8JupkBgmjc_Y?key=ML4ur5QVRGR4y2IPxSTmTHfr)

The British Museum (Image via Wikimedia Commons)

[**Róisín Lanigan: ‘I moved to London and got bedbugs’**](https://www.theguardian.com/books/2025/mar/15/roisin-lanigan-i-want-to-go-home-but-im-already-there-debut-novel?ref=the-londoner.co.uk)**— Ellen Peirson-Hagger, _Observer_**

The Observer interviewed Northern Irish writer Róisín Lanigan about all things London and renting, ahead of the release of her new novel, _I Want to Go Home But I’m Already There,_ that “remakes the haunted house genre for the rental age”.

### To Do List

🎞️ This Friday, the Prince Charles Cinema is screening potentially the most controversial movie of all time: [_Caligula: The Ultimate Cut_](https://princecharlescinema.com/film/31616696/caligula-the-ultimate-cut/?ref=the-londoner.co.uk). If you fancy enjoying a movie that upset the BBFC so much that the original print “was seized and impounded by Customs and Excise as indecent and potentially obscene”, then make sure you nab a ticket,

The duo will be discussing recent projects as diverse as the residence of the Swiss Ambassador in Algiers and the Unterfeld substation.

### **From the archive**

Footage courtesy of BBC News World Service

The Great Smog: in December 1952, an enormous cloud of air pollution enveloped London. This persisted for four days until the weather changed and the cloud dissipated. By the time it had cleared, roughly 4,000 people were estimated to have died — although more recent research suggests the real number may have been three times higher.

Tesla sales have dropped amid Elon Musk backlash. (Getty Images/Visual China Group via Getty Images)

Tesla sales have dropped amid Elon Musk backlash. (Getty Images/Visual China Group via Getty Images)

Tesla sales have plummeted by the largest drop in the company’s history. It comes amid backlash following Elon Musk’s Department of Government Efficiency (DOGE) decisions.

According to a Wednesday (2 April) [Tesla report](https://ir.tesla.com/press-release/tesla-first-quarter-2025-production-deliveries-and-deployments), sales in the electric vehicles have plummeted by 13 per cent in the first quarter of the year. This marks the largest drop in deliveries for the brand as the company navigates backlash due to chief executive officer Musk’s controversial political actions [as part of DOGE](https://www.thepinknews.com/2025/04/03/white-house-responds-elon-musk-leaving-doge-role/) and increasing competition in the EV space.

The company reported that it delivered 336,681 cars in the first three months of 2025, which is 50,000 fewer vehicles compared to the same period in 2024. The results mark the company’s worst sales in almost three years.

The sales plummet comes during a backdrop of protests and boycotts against what critics have started to call “swasticars”, a reference to Musk’s hugely controversial [Nazi-style gesture at Trump’s inauguration](https://www.thepinknews.com/2025/01/21/elon-musk-nazi-salute-donald-trump-inaugeration/).

There have also been cases of vandalism at Tesla facilities, including its charging stations and cars. The billionaire has also [reportedly lost billions from his net worth](https://www.thepinknews.com/2025/03/11/elon-musk-net-worth-tesla-stock/) since January, when the Trump-Vance administration began.

![Image 6: Tesla store front that is vandalized with bright blue paint](https://www.thepinknews.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/04/GettyImages-2207295667.jpg?w=1024)

There have been cases of vandalism at Tesla facilities. (Omer Messinger/Getty Images)

[A group called Everyone Hates Elon](https://www.thepinknews.com/2025/03/06/everyone-hates-elon-group/)has urged the public to boycott the electric car brand. In a March interview, the group told[The Hollywood Reporter](https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/news/general-news/everyone-hates-elon-musk-x-donald-trump-protest-politics-campaign-viral-1236149106/)that the incident at Trump’s inauguration gave them the impetus they needed.

“OK, Elon, if you’re going to show the world who you are, let’s show the world who Tesla really is,” a spokesperson told THR, adding that the car company’s business is where the public can best vote against the tech mogul.

Tesla did not speak about the protests against the company in its sales statement. However, it did mention an update to the Model Y car during the quarter, which temporarily paused production at four of its factories for a period of a few weeks.

**イーロン・マスク氏の過激な言動が、電気自動車（EV）大手テスラのブランドイメージに深刻な影響を及ぼし始めている。SNSではテスラ車を、ナチスドイツのシンボルとして知られる、かぎ十字「スワスティカ」になぞらえて「スワスティ・カー」と呼ぶパロディが拡散。欧州では活動家やポーランド観光相が不買運動を呼びかける事態に発展している。**

（楠 佳那子：フリー・テレビディレクター）

トランプ政権のもと新設された政府効率化省（DOGE）を率い、多忙を極めているはずの富豪のイーロン・マスク氏。そのマスク氏傘下のEV大手テスラが、最近新型モデルを発表したというパロディがSNSで広がっている。その名も「スワスティ・カー #SwastiCar」。ナチスドイツのシンボルとして知られるかぎ十字「スワスティカ」をもじった名前だ。

現在、SNSには#SwastiCarに関するジョークやミームがあふれかえっている。

80年あまり前に死亡したヒトラー総統までもが制服姿でこのスワスティ・カーの運転席に座った画像も散見される。ドイツ帝国の行末を案じているのか、かなり神妙な面持ちでハンドルを握るヒトラー氏。画像キャプションには「ここにも一人ご満悦な顧客」とある。

ギアやタイヤがかぎ十字形にデザインされている画像もある。そんなクルマがあれば、「往年の極右ファン」にはたまらないモデルとなり得るだろう。

マスク氏はトランプ大統領の就任式で、ナチスドイツ式の敬礼のようなジェスチャーをしたり、総選挙を控えたドイツで極右政党を大々的に支援したりしている。パロディはそのようなマスク氏の行動を受けてマスク氏をナチスそのものにたとえ、同氏の販売するクルマは「ナチス・カー」と揶揄（やゆ）するものである。

![Image 11](https://jbpress.ismcdn.jp/mwimgs/b/4/600mw/img_b44f2b53c076032214b9a97a0bb720f85486891.jpg)ドイツで広がる反極右・反マスク氏の声（写真：ロイター/アフロ）

ギャラリーページへ

英国では活動家らが、敬礼を想起させるマスク氏のジェスチャーの絵に「スワスティ・カーを買うな」と記したステッカーをロンドンの路上のテスラ車に貼りまくる運動を展開している。この活動を始めたとされる「みんなイーロン大嫌い #人々vsマスク」というSNSアカウントでは、サイトに登録するとアンチ・スワスティ・カーステッカーを無料でもらえる。また、彼らはマスク氏がXに投稿するごとに1ペンスを寄付すれば、マスク氏が忌み嫌う反差別・反ファシスト団体にまとめて寄付するとしている。

[米ニューズウィーク](https://www.newsweek.com/activists-brand-tesla-vehicles-swasticar-stickers-2023645)によれば、1月26日に始まったばかりのこのキャンペーンで、わずか数日のうちに5万ポンドもの寄付が集まったという。団体のサイトには米国やオーストラリアなどの人々が「ステッカーを海外にも提供して欲しい！」という投稿が並ぶ。

SNSにはこの他にも、テスラの看板の下に「ファシストF—-Off」と落書きされた画像が投稿され、それにテスラやマスク氏に対する誹謗中傷ともいえる返信が大量につくといった状況になっている。

以前なら、こうした投稿はSNSから削除されていたかもしれない。しかし、言論の自由の絶対主義者を標榜するマスク氏は、自身が所有するXから投稿を管理するモデレーターを削減し、自らヘイトや偽情報を野放しにしている。フェイスブックやインスタグラムを運営するメタのザッカーバーグCEOも、最近トランプ氏に迎合してファクトチェック機能を放棄するなどした。いずれも「ダブルスタンダード」とのそしりを受けずに、こうした投稿を取り締まることはできないだろう。

What started with a poster plastered on a bus stop in east London describing Tesla as “The Swasticar” has expanded to a series of parody advertising posters garnering millions of views on social media. The initial poster featured an image of Musk delivering his US presidential Inauguration Day ‘Nazi’ salute while riding in a Tesla accompanied by the slogan: “Goes from 0 to 1939 in 3 seconds.” Since then, ‘swasticar’ stickers have been placed on Teslas and posters have been placed on public transport proclaiming that “Hate doesn’t sell. Just ask Tesla”. The group has also targeted Musk’s social media platform X with posters urging users to “Delete your account. If the bar lets Nazis in, it’s a Nazi bar”. The campaign comes as year-on-year combined sales of Tesla Model Y and Model 3 EVs plummeted 71.9 per cent in February, compared to the same month a year earlier. According to the Electric Vehicle Council, Tesla sold just 1592 vehicles in Australia in February, down from 5665 the same time last year. The downward trend is global, as Europe experienced a 45 per cent drop in sales for January, with 9945 vehicles sold compared to 18,161 last year. The EHE group has a GoFundMe page where proceeds go to the costs of campaigning against the tech mogul and Donald Trump’s efficiency tzar. ![Image 3: Musk](https://wp.thenewdaily.com.au/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/1741143076-EHE-Musk-2.jpg?resize=1024%2C576?w=1024quality=90) As well as Teslas, the group has targeted the X social media platform._Photo: EHE_ You Might Like [![Image 4: Australia’s sales of big cars are out of control](https://wp.thenewdaily.com.au/wp-content/uploads/2025/12/1764545985-suvs.jpg?w=1024?resize=140,140&quality=90) Australia’s sales of big cars are out of control](https://www.thenewdaily.com.au/life/auto/2025/12/01/australia-big-car-problem) [![Image 5: Speedway car crashes into crowd, injuring 13 people](https://wp.thenewdaily.com.au/wp-content/uploads/2025/11/1763235034-Speedway-two-edit.jpg?w=1024?resize=140,140&quality=90) Speedway car crashes into crowd, injuring 13 people](https://www.thenewdaily.com.au/life/auto/2025/11/16/speedway-crash-crowd-nsw) Its statement on the fundraiser read: “Not happy with fuelling the far-right in the USA, Elon Musk is now doing the same in Europe. We can’t let the richest man in the world poison our politics. While nurses use food banks, his wealth grew by $200 billion last year.” It continues: “We’ve plastered ‘don’t buy a swasticar’ stickers across hundreds of Teslas in London and taken a cardboard cutout of Elon Musk to a Tesla dealership …” It has so far raised more than £4300 pounds ($A8800). Musk has repeatedly attacked British Prime Minister Keir Starmer over freedom of speech and other issues. He is also a vocal and persistent supporter of far-right politics, posting content such as “From MAGA to MEGA: Make Europe Great Again!” and endorsing Germany and Britain’s far-right parties. In an interview with [_The Hollywood Reporter_](https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/news/general-news/everyone-hates-elon-musk-x-donald-trump-protest-politics-campaign-viral-1236149106/), an EHE organiser who wished to remain anonymous said the group’s campaign started amid frustration with Musk’s provocative social media posts meddling in British and European politics. “[Musk] is the richest person in the world,” the EHE spokesperson said. “He’s got $200 billion richer last year while nurses in this country have to use food banks. And he thinks he’s got a right to talk about what British people need or want.” The EHE campaign aside, many believe that Musk’s pivot to far-right politics is fuelling a shift away from the Tesla brand. “Owning a Tesla may no longer signal purely [a buyer’s] beliefs about sustainability. There may be a nod to political or ideological affiliations that do not align with their own,” James Obiegbu and Gretchen Larsen[wrote last month.](https://www.thenewdaily.com.au/life/auto/2025/02/12/teslas-drop-elon-musk) They pointed to a recent trend of Tesla owners placing [apology stickers](https://heatmap.news/electric-vehicles/anti-elon-bumper-sticker-tesla) on their vehicles as a way of negotiating the tension between owning one of the EVs and the behaviour of a CEO they do not agree with. Meanwhile, a Facebook group for Tesla Cybertruck owners – Cybertruck Owners Only – is full of videos and photos of passersby and other drivers rudely gesturing to them, leaving notes that say “NAZI CAR”, kicking their cars and even throwing slices of cheese at it. Why do fake Elon Musk ads keep appearing around London and on the Tube?
=======================================================================

The satirical posters are designed to take a swipe at multi-billionaire Tesla owner and world’s richest man Elon Musk


-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

[Alexander Butler](https://www.independent.co.uk/author/alexander-butler)

Sunday 16 March 2025 11:45 GMT

“[Tesla](https://www.independent.co.uk/topic/tesla): The Swasticar”, reads a poster at a bus stop [opposite Sadler’s Well Theatre](https://www.independent.co.uk/tv/news/elon-musk-tesla-just-stop-oil-protest-b2714698.html). “Autopilot for your car. Autocrat for your country.”

First appearing around [Clerkenwell](https://www.independent.co.uk/topic/clerkenwell) in February, [London](https://www.independent.co.uk/topic/london) has since been plastered with guerrilla advertisements [comparing Elon Musk to a Nazi](https://www.independent.co.uk/news/world/americas/tesla-sales-slump-vandalism-dealership-musk-b2715032.html) over recent weeks.

It was a satirical swipe at the [multi-billionaire Tesla owner](https://www.independent.co.uk/news/world/americas/us-politics/trump-buy-tesla-musk-doge-b2712762.html) and world’s richest man. “We are holding Elon to account,” the group behind the poster said.

![Image 5: Posters taking a swipe at Elon Musk have appeared across London over recent weeks](https://static.independent.co.uk/2025/03/13/9/34/Everyone-Hates-Elon-Protest-Group-Continue-Their-Guerilla-Campaign-Against-Trumps-Favourite-Tech-Bro.jpeg)

open image in gallery

Posters taking a swipe at Elon Musk have appeared across London over recent weeks (Getty Images)

“Not happy with fuelling the far-right in the [USA](https://www.independent.co.uk/topic/usa), Elon Musk is now doing the same in [Europe](https://www.independent.co.uk/topic/europe). We can’t let the richest man in the world poison our politics,” it said.

Since then, copy-cat campaign groups have taken to erecting larger-scale billboard-style posters across other parts of the capital.

Here, _The Independent_ takes a look at who is behind the campaigns and why they are appearing across London.

![Image 6: The satirical posters appeared in Clerkenwell in February and have since spread across London](https://static.independent.co.uk/2025/03/14/11/42/SEI243609339-(1).jpeg)

open image in gallery

The satirical posters appeared in Clerkenwell in February and have since spread across London (Everybody Hates Elon)

Who is behind the campaigns?
----------------------------

Though it is not clear who the individuals are behind the groups, Everybody Hates Elon has vowed to “build a movement against billionaires” who “seek to divide ordinary people”.

“Everyone Hates Elon is doing actions holding Elon to account. All proceeds will go directly towards the costs of our campaigning,” the group said on its gofundme page.

Overthrow Musk said it was founded to “fight the oligarchs” and “defend democracy”, with their political stunts cropping up in Tottenham, Walthamstow and St Albans.

![Image 7: A billboard-style advert popped up in Walthamstow this week](https://static.independent.co.uk/2025/03/14/14/23/Gl6BzPPXEAAKKfz.jpeg)

open image in gallery

A billboard-style advert popped up in Walthamstow this week (Overthrow Musk)

Everybody Hates Elon was the first group reported to have erected the posters, which appeared in February.

A week later, the volunteer-led campaign group put up a series of fake advertisements on the London Underground comparing Musk to a Nazi.

It showed Musk appearing to give a Nazi salute next to Tesla’s dwindling share prices with the title: “Hate doesn’t sell. Just ask Tesla”.

A different poster showed an image of a fake “Elon’s Musk” swastika perfume bottle with the caption “Elon’s Musk, Parfum de 1939”.

![Image 8: A mock film advertisement for The Fast and Führer showing a Doge plated Telsa Model S next to the caption Heil Tesla was also put up in Tottenham](https://static.independent.co.uk/2025/03/14/14/35/Gl3JIFVbYAQKuWc.jpeg)

open image in gallery

A mock film advertisement for The Fast and Führer showing a Doge plated Telsa Model S next to the caption Heil Tesla was also put up in Tottenham (Overthrow Musk)

In Walthamstow, a billboard-style poster designed by a separate group Overthrow Musk showed an image of Musk with the words: “Buying a Tesla? You may be in for a Nazi surprise?”.

A mock film advertisement for “The Fast and Führer” showing a “Doge” plated Telsa Model S next to the caption “Heil Tesla” was also put up in Tottenham.

It had a fake PG warning reading: “Parental guidance. Tesla’s CEO is a far-right activist. Don’t give him your money.”

Why are they appearing?
-----------------------

Elon Musk was accused of giving what appeared to be a Nazi “salute” during a Trump inauguration rally in January. In response he said on X: “Frankly, they need better dirty tricks. [The “everyone is Hitler” attack is so tired.”](https://www.independent.co.uk/news/world/americas/us-politics/elon-musk-salute-trump-inauguration-b2683095.html)

Musk has made a number of high-profile attacks against Sir Keir Starmer and the Labour government, while throwing support behind right-wing party Reform.

![Image 9: Musk’s controversial salute at Trump’s inauguration parade](https://static.independent.co.uk/2025/01/21/08/elon-musk-heil-salute-far-right.jpg)

open image in gallery

Musk’s controversial salute at Trump’s inauguration parade (Getty Images)

In a slew of attacks in January, he accused the prime minister of being “complicit” in the [crimes carried out by UK grooming gangs](https://www.independent.co.uk/news/uk/politics/grooming-gangs-lisa-nandy-elon-musk-b2681392.html).

It also emerged that Musk had discussed how best to remove from office before the next UK general election.

_The Financial Times_ reported he was in talks with right-wing allies on how he could best destabilise the Labour government beyond his aggressive social media attacks on the PM.

The SpaceX and Tesla owner also took aim at Germany ahead of federal elections in February, endorsing and [promoting the far-right AfD](https://www.independent.co.uk/news/world/europe/elon-musk-afd-germany-election-b2702851.html), which came second in the polls.

Dan, who designs posters for Overthrow Musk, and only gave his first name, told _The Independent_: “Musk is an oligarch co-president. He is a very dangerous man and his Nazi salute and support for far-right European parties show this.

“But his weak spot is Tesla. His wealth is tied up in it. Reducing Tesla’s sales reduces his power. We are trying to make the link between Tesla and Musk more obvious.

What has the response been?
---------------------------

Everyone Hates Elon group is aiming to "piss Elon Musk off, one small action at a time"

An anti-Elon Musk guerrilla campaign by a UK-based group named “Everyone Hates Elon” (EHE) is going viral on social media, as people share photos of their posters online.

Everyone Hates Elon has used unconventional marketing tactics to spread their disdain for the controversial tech billionaire throughout London, with their message now spreading beyond the capital city.

The campaign gained attention after a bus stop poster was put up in east London. The poster described Tesla as “The Swasticar,” alongside an image of Musk making what appears to be a Nazi salute while riding in a Tesla. The text on the poster read: “Goes from 0 to 1939 in 3 seconds.”

The controversial tech entrepreneur caused a storm that is yet to show any signs of abating after making gestures at an event marking Donald Trump’s inauguration on Monday (20 January), which many people have likened to a[Nazi salute](https://www.thepinknews.com/2025/01/21/elon-musk-nazi-salute-donald-trump-inaugeration/).

After telling voters “thank you for making it happen”, in reference to Trump’s victory over Democrat Kamala Harris, Musk placed one hand on his chest before thrusting the other towards the crowd, his fingers together and palm turned down. He then turned and performed the same salute to the American flag.

Elon Musk denied that his gesture was a fascist salute. “Frankly, they need better dirty tricks. The ‘everyone is Hitler’ attack is so tired,” he wrote on X.

![Image 8: Elon Musk lifting his arm in the air](https://www.thepinknews.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/01/Elon-Musk-2.jpg?w=1024)

Elon Musk gives an alleged Nazi salute during a speech. (ANGELA WEISS/AFP via Getty Images)

In an interview earlier this month, the group told[The Hollywood Reporter](https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/news/general-news/everyone-hates-elon-musk-x-donald-trump-protest-politics-campaign-viral-1236149106/)that the incident at Trump’s inauguration gave them the impetus they needed. “OK, Elon, if you’re going to show the world who you are, let’s show the world who Tesla really is,” a spokesperson told THR, adding that the car company’s business is where the public can best vote against the tech mogul.

EHE’s campaign has also seen[“swasticar” stickers](https://www.thenewdaily.com.au/life/auto/2025/03/06/everyone-hates-elon)slapped on Teslas. The group have even taken to attacking Musk’s X platform, with a poster that reads: “Delete your account. If the bar lets Nazis in, it’s a Nazi bar”.

Criticism of Elon Musk has been gradually growing in volume, fuelled by the actions taken by his controversial government department, DOGE (the Department Of Government Efficiency), including [closing down USAID](https://www.thepinknews.com/2025/02/03/usaid-website-down-shut-down-elon-musk-donald-trump/). USAID is the world’s largest provider of food assistance.[Its entire website](https://www.usaid.gov/)is offline at the time of writing.

USAID leaders fought against the decision, warning Trump in memos that the closure of the agency would mean a million children will go untreated for severe malnutrition, up to 166,000 people will die from malaria and 200,000 more children will be paralyzed by polio. The programmes were cut anyway, reports [ProPublica](https://www.propublica.org/article/trump-doge-rubio-usaid-musk-death-toll-malaria-polio-tuberculosis). 

This week, people on social media ridiculed a resurfaced 2021 photo of Elon Musk, joking that [“he looks like a non-binary barista”](https://www.thepinknews.com/2025/03/06/elon-musk-hair-cut/)(among other things) because of his unusual hair cut.

Also, over the weekend, a caricature of the billionaire featured on a [carnival float at a German parade](https://www.thepinknews.com/2025/03/04/elon-musk-germany-afd/), where he was depicted wearing a nappy, holding a swastika flag and carrying a poo-filled megaphone.
